newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Iran applies to join WTO but bid stalled.
newsitem.headline: Iran applies to join WTO but bid stalled.

text.p: Iran has quietly applied to join the World Trade Organisation, but Western states are blocking its bid, trade officials in Geneva said Thursday.
They said Iran requested accession to the global trade watchdog late in September. Membership ensures access to global markets and requires following WTO rules governing trade.
But officials said there was opposition by Western governments to Tehran's request.

Normally the WTO general council would consider the application and decide to establish a working party to start the process of negotiating the terms of an accession protocol. The process can take years -- depending on the country's degree of trade liberalisation and political sensitivity.
WTO officials confirmed that the application had been received from Tehran but said there was no timetable for a decision by the ruling general council.
Iran's request would not be on the agenda of a Nov. 7 meeting of the WTO in preparation for a ministerial meeting in Singapore in December, they added.
WTO's current 125 members pledge to grant each other "most favoured nation," or equal and non-discriminatory, treatment. There are 31 countries with applications pending to join.

The United States imposed a trade and investment ban on Iran in June 1995, accusing it of sponsoring terrorism and seeking to develop nuclear weapons. Iran denies the charges and says the United States is bent on destroying the Islamic government.
A U.S. law in effect since August tightened the sanctions to include non-U.S. firms.
Washington broke diplomatic ties with Iran in 1980 after the seizure of the U.S. embassy in Tehran by Moslem militants in which 52 Americans were held hostage for 444 days.
